claims.text: Laser surface texturing can produce controlled micro-dimple arrays on the CoCrFeNi sliding surface.
Laser-textured micro-dimple arrays will promote formation of an adaptive, debris-assisted tribofilm on CoCrFeNi.
The tribofilm generated by surface texturing will significantly reduce friction from room temperature to 800 °C relative to an untreated flat CoCrFeNi surface.
The tribofilm generated by surface texturing will significantly reduce wear from room temperature to 800 °C relative to an untreated flat CoCrFeNi surface.
Flat, unmodified CoCrFeNi exhibits higher friction and wear under sliding than the proposed textured material.
An optimized combination of dimple density, depth, and spacing can reliably promote tribofilm development.
The proposed texturing is effective during ambient-atmosphere sliding at room temperature through 800 °C and approximately 0.8–1 GPa contact pressure.
Micro-dimples act as reservoirs for wear debris and oxidation products.
Retention of wear debris and oxidation products in the dimples facilitates formation and retention of a continuous tribofilm.
Micro-dimples reduce the effective contact area.
Trapped wear debris enhances local surface reactions that promote formation of a lubricious tribofilm.
The resulting tribofilm adapts to changes in temperature and load.
Adaptation of the tribofilm to temperature and load maintains low friction throughout the proposed operating range.
Adaptation of the tribofilm to temperature and load mitigates wear throughout the proposed operating range.
The intervention's performance in extreme chemical environments or under loads above the specified range is uncertain.
Sliding speed, load-dependent debris generation, and film-formation dynamics may affect tribological performance.
